messages:
anya: Heads-up — ran into a regression on prod: GQA kernel picks for short sequences spike tail latency when KV-cache is paged with 64B blocks.

sam: Hmm. Is that the same fallback we saw last month or a new behavior?

anya: New. We've been seeing a particular pattern: when user seq_len <= 32 and cache fragmentation > 0.7, the kernel selector prefers the GQA wide-block path which ends up doing extra memcopy for paged kv stripes. Latency goes up ~20-30% p50->p95.

perf-bot: Automatic profile attached: p95 increased from 56ms -> 74ms for short seqs on ecs-a100-48. KV fragmentation metric crossed threshold at 0.72.

mike: Do you have a quick repro? Can we get a tiny profile snippet?

anya: Paste of the tight reproducer run:
```
# run on testbox (a100)
./runner --model t5-small --mode gqa --seq 24 --bat 8 --kv-page 64 --iter 200
Summary: mean=42.1ms p95=73.9ms
Kernel picks: 80% gqa_blockwide, 20% mqa_compact
KV: pages=128 frag=0.74 avg_page_fill=0.31
```

lucy: That avg_page_fill is low — lots of small fills. GQA wide-block assumes contiguous KV mapping so memcopy costs spike. In MQA we do smaller kernels and less memcpy. Selector should tilt away from gqa in this region.

sam: Agreed. Two quick ideas: 1) add a frag-aware penalty in kernel_score for small seq lengths, 2) teach autotuner to sample seq_len distribution and prefer MQA when avg_page_fill < 0.5.

anya: I prototyped a frag-penalty formula: score' = score - alpha * frag * (1 - min(1, seq_len/64)). With alpha=0.45 it's already switching picks on the testbox.

mike: Nice. How does that behave on high-throughput batches? Any cost to throughput when seq_len>128?

anya: On long seqs no ops change — multiplier is near zero so we keep current GQA picks. I also added a small hysteresis window so we don't flip-flop under noisy frag estimates.

lucy: We should be careful with per-request frag reading; add a running-window histogram per worker instead. Sampling every N requests.

sam: Also want to evaluate batching heuristics: when we see many short seqs but mixed frag, continuous batching can increase average frag because it pulls in different traces. Maybe prefer micro-batches for paged layouts.

anya: Good point. On the repro I toggled micro_batching=true and p95 dropped 10% more. Suggestion: add a policy rule: if avg_page_fill < 0.5 and seq_len_median < 48 then prefer micro-batches up to 4.

perf-bot: Quick simulation: applying frag-penalty + micro-batch policy yields p95 62ms in sim, saves ~14% tokens/s in best-case throughput but keeps p95 inside SLO.

mike: Tradeoff seems acceptable for latency-sensitive routes. We should gate by route-level SLO and customer tier.

lucy: For autotuner: we should extend the sampling matrix to include (seq_len_bucket, page_fill_bucket, arch) and record kernel latency delta. Then the offline scoring job can fit a small model to predict expected delta and emit per-arch thresholds.

sam: Yup — also track hotcache hit ratio; when hotcache>0.6 the frag penalty should be reduced because cached prefixes hide some memcpy.

anya: Plan: 1) land frag-penalty + hysteresis in kernel-selector (small flag), 2) add micro-batch policy toggles, 3) extend autotuner sampler to log page_fill histograms + kernel deltas. I'll open a PR with test vectors.

mike: Can you include a tiny benchmark matrix in the PR covering seq_len {16,32,64,256} x page_fill {0.25,0.5,0.75} on both a100 and h100?

anya: Yep — will run this afternoon and post results here.

sam: Also add a regression test that simulates a cache-frag spike so selector can't regress silently.

lucy: If we want to be defensive, add a runtime fallback: if p95 increases >15% after deploy for a specific route, auto-fallback to MQA for that route for 10 minutes while we investigate.

anya: Good call. I'll prototype the fallback in the rollout policy.

mike: Thanks team. Low-risk incremental change, looks actionable. Ping once PR is up and we can schedule a quick canary. :thumbsup:
